defects: Adds hypothesis [Field S] not present in gold, which only assumes CommRing S with IsFractionRing R S (no IsDomain R is required in gold, so S need not be a field in the general setting gold covers); this narrows the class of rings the theorem applies to.

Adds hypothesis [Module.Free R N] not present in gold; gold's rank equality holds without N being free over R (e.g. N = ℚ as a ℤ-module is not free, yet the classical fact finrank_ℚ(ℚ)=finrank_ℤ(ℚ) still holds), so this is a genuine unnecessary strengthening.

Adds hypothesis [Module.Finite S N] not present in gold; gold's finrank-based statement holds unconditionally (using the junk value 0 in the infinite-dimensional case), while produced restricts to the finite-dimensional case only.

Conclusion is reformulated asymmetrically as Module.rank R N = (finrank S N : Cardinal) instead of gold's finrank S N = finrank R N; this is only equivalent to gold under the added finiteness/freeness hypotheses, so it does not capture the same general proposition as gold.
Uses [AddCommMonoid N] instead of gold's [AddCommGroup N] (mathematically implied given the ring module structure, but a differently-shaped hypothesis).
